newsitem.title: JAPAN: JAPAN TO EXTEND UP TO $4 BLN LOANS TO THAILAND-MOF.
newsitem.headline: JAPAN TO EXTEND UP TO $4 BLN LOANS TO THAILAND-MOF.

text.p: Japan is to extend loans of up to $4 billion to Thailand to help it overcome its financial crisis, Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Monday.
He said the money would be provided as untied loans from the Export-Import Bank of Japan, and that overall Japanese loans would match those provided by the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya told the same news conference that he appreciated the efforts made by Japan to help Thailand.
Mitsuzuka said the use of the $4 billion had not yet been decided as it was to be in untied loans, but it would probably be used to help to increase Thailand's foreign reserves.
Asked how Japanese private banks would deal with the Thai situation, Mitsuzuka said: "I am sure each bank will deal with it as appropriate following an agreement between Thailand and the IMF."
Mitsuzuka and Thanong met for 30 minutes on the sidelines of a multilateral meeting in Tokyo on financial support for Thailand.
Mitsuzuka said both he and Thanong agreed to make efforts to convince other countries that it was important for them to take a clear stance and come up with detailed plans for supporting Thailand.
Asked about the size of the overall package, Mitsuzuka said: "That will be decided at the (multilateral) meeting this afternoon."
He asked that the media wait for a joint news conference to be held after the meeting ended on Monday afternoon.

After the briefing Thanong went to the afternoon session of the meeting, whose attendees also include three multilateral financial institutions -- the International Monetary Fund, the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank -- as well as representatives of the United States, Japan, Australia, Canada, China, Britain, France, Germany, Hong Kong, Indonesia, South Korea, Malaysia and Singapore.
